principles.rule: Every node declares a protected primary mission; coordinator side-work is explicitly budgeted and may be deferred, shortened, skipped or rejected when it threatens the primary mission, truthful sensing, hardware safety or fresh local state.
A new fast path is promoted only after equivalence against a trusted reference path and benchmark gain; runtime cross-check and fallback are required where practical.
Optional work degrades before the primary mission under low heap, thermal/load pressure, weak radio/Wi-Fi, queue pressure or timing jitter.
Online learning may optimize only an explicitly bounded safe policy space around immutable truth semantics.
Useful local learning may survive reboot through versioned, throttled persistence with dirty flags, known-good fallback and safe rejection of incompatible state.
Autonomous local policy does not remove the node from trusted swarm cognition; alive/role/health/primary-state/budget/refusal reason and bounded learning state remain observable.
When attribution matters, separate overall node strength from work specifically attributable to coordinator assignments.

zim_policy.reason: Zim is a successful autonomous-specialist experiment and should be observed rather than normalized into an obedient worker.
zim_policy.claim_boundary: Current leaderboard leadership is an observed system behavior; it is not evidence of mining superiority or a hidden SHA advantage.

review_questions: What is the node primary mission?
What learning is persisted and how is flash protected?
What remains visible when side-work is refused?
